verdict.rationale: Zep's own Graphiti temporal graph documents a bi-temporal model with fact invalidation and tracks how facts change over time, which plausibly retires superseded facts. However, nothing shows a developer can set a TTL, assign expiration dates, or apply recency-weighted decay to retrieval. Manual node and edge deletion is only an adjacent control and earns no credit. Missing for 10: developer-configurable TTL or expiry dates on memories, recency weighting or decay in search ranking, documentation that invalidated facts are excluded from Zep Cloud retrieval, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can make memories expire or decay — via TTL, expiration dates, or recency weighting — so stale facts stop surfacing

citations.quote: entity and edge extraction, the bi-temporal model, fact invalidation, and hybrid retrieval
